#text-structuring-project #scientific-method Part 1 of 4 (delivered 2023/05/22) is titled "The Intricacies of Theories and Phenomena: A Deeper Look at the Scientific Method"; sections: Introduction, Scientific Method (prediction vs. explanation), Boundary Conditions & Hempel-Oppenheim model, Complexities (multiple propositions, stochastic sampling, data vs. findings), Conclusion. Its outline has been delivered.

#scientific-method Prediction vs. explanation: prediction derives a finding from a theory and later observes the phenomenon; explanation observes first, then derives. Same logical structure, differing epistemic order of derivation and observation.

#scientific-method Boundary conditions are the link between general, rule-like theories (all-quantified or probabilistically qualified propositions) and singular findings in the deductive-nomological method. Hempel-Oppenheim model: general laws plus specific boundary conditions jointly derive an empirical finding.

#scientific-method Complexity 1: a theory is typically a set of multiple propositions, not a single proposition. Complexity 2: observations/data are often produced by stochastic sampling (e.g., a population-level mean reaction-time difference observed via a finite sample).

#scientific-method Data vs. finding: in the Big Five personality-traits/political-attitudes questionnaire study, the raw questionnaire responses are the data; the resulting correlation is the finding.
